1.1: Burden of Nineveh. The Book of the Vision of Nahum the Elkoshite.
1.2: A God zealous and avenging is Jehovah, An avenger is Jehovah, and possessing fury. An avenger is Jehovah on His adversaries, And He is watching for His enemies.
1.3: Jehovah is slow to anger, and great in power, And Jehovah does not entirely acquit, In a hurricane and in a tempest is His way, And a cloud is the dust of His feet.
1.4: He is pushing against a sea, and dries it up, Yes, all the floods He has made dry, Languishing are Bashan and Carmel, Yes, the flower of Lebanon is languishing.
1.5: Mountains have shaken because of Him, And the hills have been melted; And lifted up is the earth at His presence, And the world and all dwelling in it.
1.6: Before His indignation who does stand? And who rises up in the heat of His anger? His fury has been poured out like fire, And the rocks have been broken by Him.
1.7: Good is Jehovah for a strong place in a day of distress. And He knows those trusting in Him.
1.8: And with a flood passing over, An end He makes of its place, And His enemies does darkness pursue.
1.9: What do we devise against Jehovah? An end He is making, arise not twice does distress.
1.10: For while princes are perplexed, And with their drink are drunken, They have been consumed as stubble fully dried.
1.11: From you has come forth a deviser of evil Against Jehovah--a worthless counsellor.
1.12: Thus said Jehovah: Though complete, and thus many, Yet thus they have been cut off, And he has passed away. And I afflicted you, I afflict you no more.
1.13: And now I break his rod from off you, And your bands I do draw away.
1.14: And commanded concerning you has Jehovah, `No more of your name does spread abroad, From the house of your gods I cut off graven and molten image, I appoint your grave, for you have been vile.
1.15: Indeed, on the mountains the feet of one proclaiming tidings, sounding peace! Celebrate, O Judah, your festivals, complete your vows, For add no more to pass over into you does the worthless, He has been completely cut off!

2.1: Come up has a scatterer to your face, Keep the bulwark, watch the way, Strengthen the loins, strengthen power mightily.
2.2: For turned back has Jehovah to the excellency of Jacob, As to the excellency of Israel, For emptied them out have emptiers, And their branches they have marred.
2.3: The shield of his mighty ones is become red, Men of might are in scarlet, With fiery torches is the chariot in a day of his preparation, And the firs have been caused to tremble.
2.4: In out-places shine do the chariots, They go to and fro in broad places, Their appearances are like torches, As lightnings they run.
2.5: He does remember his honourable ones, They stumble in their goings, They hasten to its wall, and prepared is the covering.
2.6: Gates of the rivers have been opened, And the palace is dissolved.
2.7: And it is established--she has removed, She has been brought up, And her handmaids are leading as the voice of doves, Tabering on their hearts.
2.8: And Nineveh is as a pool of waters, From of old it is --and they are fleeing! `Stand you, stand;' and none is turning!
2.9: Seize you silver, seize you gold, And there is no end to the prepared things, To the abundance of all desirable vessels.
2.10: She is empty, yes, emptiness and waste, And the heart has melted, And the knees have smitten together, And great pain is in all loins, And the faces of all of them have gathered paleness.
2.11: Where is the habitation of lionesses? And a feeding-place it is for young lions Where walked has a lion, an old lion, A lion's whelp, and there is none troubling.
2.12: The lion is tearing parts for his whelps, And is strangling for his lionesses, And he does fill with prey his holes, And his habitations with rapine.
2.13: Indeed, I am against you, An affirmation of Jehovah of Hosts, And I have burned in smoke its chariot, And your young lions consume does a sword, And I have cut off from the land your prey, And not heard any more is the voice of your messengers!

3.1: Woe to the city of blood, She is all with lies--burglary--full, Prey does not depart.
3.2: The sound of a whip, And the sound of the rattling of a wheel, And of a prancing horse, and of a bounding chariot, Of a horseman mounting.
3.3: And the flame of a sword, and the lightning of a spear, And the abundance of the wounded, And the weight of carcases, Yes, there is no end to the bodies, They stumble over their bodies.
3.4: Because of the abundance of the fornications of an harlot, The goodness of the grace of the lady of witchcrafts, Who is selling nations by her fornications, And families by her witchcrafts.
3.5: Indeed, I am against you, An affirmation of Jehovah of Hosts, And have removed your skirts before your face, And have showed nations your nakedness, And kingdoms your shame,
3.6: And I have cast upon you abominations, And dishonoured you, and made you as a sight.
3.7: And it has come to pass, Each of your beholders flees from you, And has said: `Spoiled is Nineveh, Who does bemoan for her?' From where do I seek comforters for you?
3.8: Are you better than No-Ammon, That is dwelling among brooks? Waters she has round about her, Whose bulwark is the sea, waters her wall.
3.9: Cush her might, and Egypt, and there is no end. Put and Lubim have been for your help.
3.10: Even she does become an exile, She has gone into captivity, Even her sucklings are dashed to pieces At the top of all out-places, And for her honoured ones they cast a lot, And all her great ones have been bound in fetters.
3.11: Even you are drunken, you are hidden, Even you do seek a strong place, because of an enemy.
3.12: All your fortresses are fig-trees with first-fruits, If they are shaken, They have fallen into the mouth of the eater.
3.13: Indeed, your people are women in your midst, To your enemies thoroughly opened Have been the gates of your land, Consumed has fire your bars.
3.14: Waters of a siege draw for yourself, Strengthen your fortresses, Enter into mire, and tread on clay, Make strong a brick-kiln.
3.15: There consume you does a fire, Cut you off does a sword, It does consume you as a cankerworm! Make yourself heavy as the cankerworm, Make yourself heavy as the locust.
3.16: Multiply your merchants above the stars of the heavens, The cankerworm has stripped off, and does flee away.
3.17: Your crowned ones are as a locust, And your princes as great grasshoppers, That encamp in hedges in a day of cold, The sun has risen, and it does flee away, And not known is its place where they are.
3.18: Slumbered have your friends, king of Asshur, Rest do your honourable ones, Scattered have been your people on the mountains, And there is none gathering.
3.19: There is no weakening of your destruction, Grievous is your smiting, All hearing your fame have clapped the hand at you, For over whom did not your wickedness pass continually?
